profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer @ Atlassian
profile.summary:
Hey there, I'm Kari. I'm a product-focused software engineer with a background in backend development.

I love building products that solve real user problems: I bring a strong customer intuition to the forefront of the work that I do, and I’m always refining that intuition with data. I seek to understand the big picture and historical context and leverage that understanding to ensure that the “how” and “what” we’re building align with the “why” in order to focus on what matters most.

I care deeply about creating sustainable systems, whether that’s resilient engineering products and infrastructure or team processes that scale and support long term team health and well being. The campsite rule — leave it better than you found it — guides my approach to work, whether it’s code, people, or processes. 

I do my best work in communicative, collaborative, and creative teams that take high levels of ownership and investment in what they deliver. 

On a personal note, I'm happiest when I'm learning —  I'm a photographer/videographer, Latin dancer, powerlifter, reader, and occasional skier.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Building a 0>1>100 product at Atlassian for strategic leaders, designed to provide visibility into company strategy and connect strategy to execution.

positions.title: Software Engineer II
positions.description: Engineer on a platform team that built and maintained a Tier 1 service that managed IAM access to all of VMware's tens of thousands of cloud accounts at scale, and enabled users to deploy infrastructure to public cloud (AWS, Azure, and GCP) accounts.

educations.schoolName: California Polytechnic State University-San Luis Obispo

honors.title: President's List
honors.description:
Recognizes undergraduate students who have demonstrated consistent achievement, as represented by being named on the Dean's Honors List - completed 12 or more letter-graded units at Cal Poly during the quarter with a 3.5 grade point average or better for that term - for any three of the four quarters of the university year. 

Received President's List for school years 2016-2017, 2017-2018, 2018-2019, and 2019-2020
